values.label: context for a reader new to the subject
knows the subject already
values.note: Default value: no code, pair or candidate can show it, because both corpora hold only editions or options made for a reader with a need

values.label: key points first, full detail kept
values.note: Also advice for every reader: GB1.clear-structure (B), GB4.2011 (B)

values.label: a shorter version with the essential points
values.note: Outside factor guidance: a shorter version that holds only the essential points selects content, which kbp/0.9 and plan S3.2 keep out of factor advice, so S3 writes a no-change row. Without the 7 A1 pairs that cut content, 11 pairs from 4 publishers remain

values.label: the full detail up front
numbers with everyday words beside each figure
figures or a table in place of long text
the content as sound
reads by eye
values.note: Default value: no code, pair or candidate can show it, because both corpora hold only editions or options made for a reader with a need

values.label: less motion
values.note: N17 less-motion holds the motion evidence that N9 held before the review pass; 1 situation candidate (grade C)

values.label: no motion preference
values.literature_evidence: SA6 (B) defines the no-preference value; EV10 (B) shows animated transitions helping 24 adults track change
values.note: Default value, the registry's no-preference; no code, pair or candidate can show it, because both corpora hold only editions or options made for a reader with a need

values.label: everyday words and short sentences
meaning stated outright
pictures beside the words
few distractions
values.note: N9 keeps distractions without motion; the 5 motion options and SC-095 moved to N17

values.label: a familiar, consistent layout
values.note: COGA states the need for interfaces

values.label: a way to find and read only the parts that matter
small chunks with clear space between
values.note: No factor: segmenting gains for every reader across 56 investigations (EV5c, B, meta-analysis), so the value stands as advice for every reader (plan question 5)

values.label: a way to find and pick the version that suits the reader
values.note: No factor: offering several editions and a way to pick one is a publishing choice; in a knowledge base the reader's factor values already pick the presentation

values.label: a copy to go over again later
values.note: No factor: a copy to return to is a delivery question, and a knowledge-base document already stays available; the presentation part, written beside spoken, sits under F4

values.label: reads the language as a second language
takes in long material slowly
values.note: Calls for V2a or V2b in the source

values.label: comes from outside the field
reads on a small screen or in limited space
values.note: Calls for V2a: a short layer with the detail one link away (GB8.methods)

values.label: reads only a short version unless a point matters
reads with someone who talks the document through
mentally tired
values.note: SB9 covers total sleep deprivation only

values.label: interrupted, or loses track partway
stressed, anxious or pressed for time
on the move, or attending to something else
values.literature_evidence: SA1 (A) and SB1.review (B) name the condition; no graded source ties a document presentation to the condition

factors.name: subject-familiarity
factors.gist: How much does the reader already know about the document's subject?
factors.cond1_evidence: CS1b, CS2, EA1 (B); EV5d (B, abstract only); SA2.u-reading-level (A)
factors.cond4_note: F2 also changes the amount shown at once, for time and attention rather than subject knowledge
factors.moment_evidence: Changes as the reader learns (GB6.cognition; CS2), over weeks or months rather than from moment to moment
factors.set_by_lead: scope, thin: 2 policy rows split between scope and universe, plus the per-folder argument
factors.set_by_evidence: Pair rows cannot tell the levels apart, because every pair covers one document by the eligibility rule. Policy rows for C3 or N12: eLife digests for some articles (scope) and Cochrane summaries for every review (universe). Prior knowledge differs by subject (EV5d, abstract only), so one reader's value can differ between folders

factors.name: amount-and-order
factors.gist: How much of the document does the reader need before the detail?
factors.conditions: C2 C4 C5 C7 C8 C9 C10
factors.cond4_note: The situational conditions are reasons for F2 values, so no separate lead adjusts amount for time and attention
factors.moment_evidence: Within one reading: SC-017, SC-050, SC-073. Between readings: SC-020, SC-053. Literature: SB4, SB5, GB6.cognition, SA3 clause 5.1.4, SB1.review, SB7 (B)
factors.set_by_evidence: Pair rows cannot tell the levels apart, because every pair covers one document by the eligibility rule. SA3 (B, preview) and SA5 (B) tell the writer to find out who will use one document before writing it (instance)
factors.protocol_note: V2b (a shorter version) selects content and stays out of factor advice; reading order falls under plan question 1

factors.name: number-form
factors.gist: Which form of numbers does the reader take in most easily?

factors.name: listening
factors.gist: Does the reader take the document in by ear?
factors.moment_to_moment: no: the setting can change; no change observed
factors.moment_evidence: Help pages allow change during use for 24 of 26 audio options; no usage study found. SC-052 comes from a guide that suggests listening while travelling and reports no reader
factors.set_by_lead: gap: 2 grade C candidates point to instance
factors.set_by_evidence: SC-013 and SC-051 switch speech on only for long texts, so the value differs per document (instance); both candidates are grade C, which never forms the only basis

factors.name: less-motion
factors.gist: Has the reader asked for less motion?
factors.cond1_evidence: SA2.u-animation-from-interactions (A) and SA6 (B) against C53 (B) and C51 (B, abstract only)
factors.cond4_note: N17 holds motion and N9 holds other distractions, so F5 and F8 count separate evidence
factors.moment_to_moment: no: the setting can change; no change observed
factors.moment_evidence: SA6 (B) requires user agents to re-evaluate a changed preference, and SA1.p-o8p01 (A) asks for a setting reachable from each screen: both show the setting can change. Help pages leave change during use unclear for 10 of 11 motion options; no usage study and no situation candidate
factors.set_by_evidence: SA1.p-o8p01 (A, editor's draft): an easily available setting is set one time with as wide a scope as possible, such as the operating system (universe), or saved for a set of pages (scope)
factors.protocol_note: Motion falls under plan question 1; the values could come from the prefers-reduced-motion registry (a source-backed factor)

factors.name: everyday-wording
factors.gist: Does the reader need everyday words and meaning stated outright?
factors.cond1_evidence: GB1.clear-language (B) and GB4.writing (B) report a gain for every reader; the cost evidence (C10, C11) concerns added explanations, which F1 covers
factors.protocol_note: Advice for every reader: plan question 5

factors.name: pictures-with-words
factors.gist: Does the reader need pictures beside the words?
factors.cond1_evidence: The A and B cost evidence ties to prior knowledge (C06, C09; C45 abstract only), so F1 holds the evidence; SC-002 (B), SC-056 (C) and SC-062 (C) report readers who found pictures childish, confusing or misleading

factors.name: distractions-and-layout
factors.gist: Does the reader need few distractions and a familiar layout?
factors.cond1_evidence: SA1 states both needs for interfaces; BV4 (B, abstract only) reports a reader-view gain for every reader
factors.protocol_note: S2 decides whether interface needs apply to documents

factors.name: reads-with-a-helper
factors.gist: Does someone talk the document through with the reader?
factors.cond1_evidence: No graded source shows a cost to other readers

factors.name: find-the-part
factors.gist: Does the reader need only some parts?
factors.cond1_evidence: SA2.u-headings-and-labels (A), C41 and C46 (B, abstract only) report gains for every reader
factors.protocol_note: Advice for every reader: plan question 5

factors.name: reading-task
factors.gist: What is the reader doing with the document?
factors.cond1_evidence: C35 (B, abstract only) ties representation to the task; SA3 (B, preview) lists reading purposes; the coding rule recorded no task statements
factors.cond4_note: Content shape per section falls under plan question 3
factors.moment_evidence: SA3 (B, preview) says purpose differs by occasion
factors.protocol_note: Owner lead: content shape and the reader's task choose the format first

factors.name: learning-style
factors.gist: Matching a format to a preferred learning style
factors.exclusion: out of scope and contested: a value would label the reader's learning style; C29 (B) reports adequate studies that contradict matching; C31 (B) pools g = 0.31 to 0.32 with I2 = 91.17; C21 (B) calls full dismissal premature

factors.name: diagnosis
factors.exclusion: out of scope: values name needs or conditions; GB6.cognition (B) and SB2 (B) say the same diagnosis brings different needs

factors.name: level
factors.gist: A value naming a reading age, education level or confidence level
factors.exclusion: out of scope: rules section 3 keeps a level in the verbatim column only; C61 (C)

factors.name: style-imagery-ability
factors.gist: A value naming a cognitive style, imagery vividness or a measured ability
factors.exclusion: out of scope and unsupported: the value would assess the reader (SB2, B); C23 to C26 and C17 (B) test no presentation for such a value

factors.name: income
factors.gist: A value naming the reader's income or money worries
factors.exclusion: contested and out of scope: SB11 against SB11.audit (B); a value would label the reader's circumstances

factors.name: font-preference
factors.gist: A value naming a dyslexia font
